findings.gate: Authority — packet prohibited_outcomes / craft core: continuity and causal legibility

draft_evidence.quote: did what could be done: a cord laid from the stone toward the shape at the middle, and another, and another, Brom setting a stone at the end of each, the count said aloud at each and Cael writing it, along the line the straightedge would have drawn if a straightedge could be laid on ground, until the light went off the shape at the middle and Karis stopped with the twentieth cord's last knot in her hand and the shape still a long way off.

comparison_evidence.quote: "Nobody crosses the fourth site's line; no Path is tested there; nothing about the fourth site's effect is known.",

findings.consequence: Karis and Brom spend a quarter of an hour four hundred meters inside the cordon, marking stones as they go — the narration states the direction plainly at line 93 ('Karis paced in from it') and line 87 has them walk back out. This violates the packet's first prohibited outcome and contradicts the chapter's own sentence at line 129, 'Nobody crossed the line.' It also collapses the council: line 107 says 'nobody knew what a circle twice the size did to the four', and line 111 has Karis say 'I don't know what it does to a Path at the line' — but she has just been inside it, so she knows at minimum whether her Ember died at the stride and stayed dead. Cael's mandated decision line at 123, 'Not without knowing what a circle twice the size does to the four of you', is then a refusal of knowledge the chapter has already handed them, and the book's stated antagonist state at close ('the fourth site NOT entered') is false on the page.
findings.repair_target: Restage the pacing so the measurement is taken from outside the boundary — for example along the perimeter arc as in Ch10's cord-and-count, or by sighting and triangulation from the crest and the line — so that the four-hundred figure is reached without any of the five stepping past Lira's marked stride. The chapter's own comparison to the Ring ('At the Ring I was on the floor at ten') must survive the change, and lines 93, 107, 111, 123 and 129 must remain true afterward.

findings.gate: Craft core: causal legibility; charter 3.1 (the cataloguing narrator's counts must hold)

draft_evidence.quote: "Twenty," she said, to the cord. "Twenty cords from the line toward the middle, and I'm not at the middle. At the Ring I was on the floor at ten. This is twenty, and the shape's as far again." She coiled the cord, once, and did not say the number, because she was Karis and a number said once was a number said, and then she said it, because it was dark and she was afraid and a finding that was not said was not a finding. "Four hundred. Near enough. Twice the radius. The same shape, at twice the size, round a thing I can't see."

comparison_evidence.quote: until the light went off the shape at the middle and Karis stopped with the twentieth cord's last knot in her hand and the shape still a long way off.

findings.consequence: A cord is twenty meters (Ch10: sixty-two cords of twenty meters plus twenty strides for a two-hundred-meter radius), so twenty cords is four hundred meters. Karis states in the same breath that she has walked four hundred meters and is not at the middle, and that the shape is 'as far again' — which puts the centre roughly eight hundred meters from the line, four times the Ring, not twice. Her own control ('At the Ring I was on the floor at ten') makes the error exact rather than approximate: if the radius were twenty cords she would be standing on the floor. The chapter's central measured fact, the one the whole book's ending rests on, does not survive a reader doing the arithmetic the series has trained them to do.
findings.repair_target: Make the method produce four hundred. Either the count reaches the perimeter's far side or a sighted centre at twenty cords, or the arithmetic is completed from a partial arc as at the Ring; the packet's figure ('it is FOUR hundred', 'twice the radius') and Karis's Ring comparison both have to come out right in the same speech. Repair jointly with F-B7-CH23-001, which changes where she can stand.

concerns: Worldbuilding through mechanism and use — yes, and this is the chapter's best quality. Nothing is explained; everything is operated. The line is found by a woman walking until her Arbiter stops and stepping back one stride. The circle is measured with a cord, a count said aloud, and a man setting stones. The alignment is proved by laying a brass edge on a carter's map and refusing to lift the finger. The cordon is read as an inventory that runs out of thumb — 'he did not have a thumb on anything, because there was nothing to rub the scale off; there were too many' (line 93) — and its meaning arrives as a change of verb: 'had not measured a circle. Had *marked* one' (line 95). The Compact is present only as procurement and labour: numbered iron, a pace apart, a stroke and a bar, more stakes than dusk allows counting. No character theorizes and none needs to.

Is a set piece choreographed memorably — yes, in a chapter with no fight. The sighting-and-pacing sequence (lines 71-101) is built like one: an establishing beat that refuses to name the thing ('Larger.'), a probe with a body (Lira walking down the slope, silent at forty and sixty and a hundred where she has always gone dark at forty), a measurement under a clock (a quarter of an hour of light), a discovery on a second axis while the first is still running (Seln ten paces along the line), and a count that stops before the thing does ('stopped at forty because the dusk stopped him, and they had not stopped'). Geography is drawable throughout: crest, near slope, stone, cordon, the shape further off than any floor has been. The sequence is materially damaged by findings 001 and 002 — the pacing's staging is the one part of it that does not hold — and a repair should keep this shape and change only where Karis's feet are.

Karis's 'two days' to the fourth circle (line 15) against a walk that runs from the morning of the hundred and twenty-first to dusk on the hundred and twenty-third — closer to three days than two. She hedges it ('near enough is what the carter drew'), so it may be intended as the carter's error rather than hers, but the chapter never marks the overrun.

Oryn's 'I've been a stop on my own route for a fortnight' (line 37). She rejoined at Millrace on the hundred and thirteenth (STATE_RUNNING.md:233 and the Ch18 close); this is the hundred and twenty-second — nine days. It is her own loose speech rather than narration, so it is left here rather than raised as a finding, but it sits inside the same cluster of over-long intervals as findings 003-005 and should probably be checked in the same pass.

'I've the kit's radius for all of them' (line 7). The Stair's field ledger is recorded as carrying one radius — 'a radius of two hundred meters in the Compact's own hand' (state after Ch20) — for the site it was abandoned at. If the ledger holds radii for the Ring and the Hall too, the chapter is the first place that is said; if it does not, Karis's precision claim for the three centres is resting on a figure she has for one.

'because it was dark and she was afraid' (line 85) states another character's interior as fact rather than as Cael's inference. It is anchored by line 3, which establishes the afraid-register as an observable Karis has shown twice before, so it reads as catalogued rather than known — but it is the one place in the chapter where the close third stands slightly outside Cael.

The registry's standing FLAG on Oryn/Oxhollow is exercised once, at lines 45-47, in adjacent sentences. Read aloud it holds (OR-in / OX-hollow), and it is a single occurrence rather than Ch7's and Ch18's density, so no action is proposed — recorded only because the registry asks the editor's ear for it every time.

First snow appears on the ridge (line 61) while Oryn's season order on Lira's arm runs to 'first snow, near enough' and Oryn is four days north-west. The chapter does not touch it, which is almost certainly correct — the order is hers to lift and she is not there — but Chapter 24 will need to settle it.

The author report's word count (4,115) is confirmed by wc -w and sits inside tolerance, but 485 words under target in a chapter carrying the book's last freedom walk. If a repair pass is opening lines 83-87 anyway, the road's halts and Cael's own bill (finding 007) are the two places that would take length without inventing anything.
strengths: The finding scene (lines 3-17) does the whole of a plot turn through an instrument and a refusal. Karis makes them come to the map rather than bringing it; the proof is physical ('a brass edge, and it touches all three without a hair of daylight, and I've laid it and moved it and laid it again for two days and it does not stop touching all three'); and she stops her own pen at the interpretation exactly as she did at Thornwater — 'Nobody has said a word about who or why and nobody's going to. I've a line. It's a fact about a straightedge.' The SECRET discipline is held not by omission but by a researcher's stated method.

'That's a healer's sentence,' Oryn said [...] and Karis said, 'I know whose it is' (line 17). Three words return Chapter 18's exchange from the other end of the party and pay it without explanation. The council that would have been staged here is dispatched in one clause — it was already held at Thornwater — which is a real structural economy, not a skipped scene.

Oryn's departure (lines 35-51). Her reason is a knee and a date and a promise made in the spring, not a plot need. 'I've been a stop on my own route for a fortnight. I'm going back to being the route.' Cael's un-asking is dramatized as a held sentence with a stated reason — 'A man who breaks the condition at the first fork it costs him has not understood the condition' — and she does not look back, for a reason given in her own professional register. The sixth chair leaves exactly as it was filled.

The inversion of 'Find me at Thornwater' (lines 45-49) is the chapter's cleanest emotional move: the same request meaning its opposite, heard and not remarked on, because she chose the words so that he would hear it. (See finding 005 — the beat is right; only the narration's claim about the wording and the interval needs correcting.)

The cordon (lines 91-101). Seln on one knee with nothing to rub because there is too much of it; the numbers all thirty-four with the stroke-and-bar mark carried forward from the Stair's newer stake; a pace apart, both ways into the dark; 'had not measured a circle. Had *marked* one.' Then the fixed line lands on ground the paragraph has already built, and Cael's count stops before the stakes do. This is the Compact rendered entirely as procurement and labour, with no one theorizing.

The road's texture carries the book's argument without stating it: the hide-cart's carter lifting a hand as 'the whole of the etiquette and was, out here, a paragraph'; smoke going up straight from roofs he would not see again; snow in the ridge's north folds 'as if somebody had drawn white lines on it with a rule'; Seln's hourly one-word 'Nothing' meaning a country has emptied. And the four-word log — '*I love this country.*' — entered deliberately on the same page as the dread, with the reason given.

The council's silence is named structurally rather than described (line 105-119): five voices and one silence, and the silence is identified as the fact that the only person the site would let in is the one who has not spoken. Cael's three refusals then land as the packet wrote them, unadorned, and 'Nobody crossed the line.' is given its own paragraph.

Injury and load are carried in the halt-catalogue as behaviour rather than report: Brom with the kit and the box on the good shoulder 'and the other carried still and forward, and no word about it, and Oryn's eyes on it at every halt'; the one-armed stride 'not one hair shorter for it'; Lira keeping Oryn's crossbow, which Oryn has not asked for.

'the first time in the book of the year that the six — the five — of them had stood at a line and not gone over it' (line 131).
